newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares end down on politics worries, rates.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares end down on politics worries, rates.

text.p: Istanbul shares ended slightly lower amid political worries and overnight interest rates which remained high on Friday, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 .XU100 closed at 2,004, down 12 points, or 0.6 percent from Thursday after trading in a narrow corridor of 1,996 and 2,032.
The index dropped 1.76 percent this week compared to last week's 3.4 percent jump.
Daily volume fell 10.3 percent to 19.58 trillion lira ($120 million), from Thursday's 21.8 trillion ($133 million).

Toygar Sungur from Meksa Securities said the bearish sentiment which emerged in the afternoon session was partly due to the rejection of an article during a parliamentary debate on a bill to raise compulsory education to eight years from five.
If the bill passes, it will necessitate the closing down of the junior high sections of religious schools. The first four articles were accepted in debates which began on Thursday.
The debate is seen as the latest stage in the political fight between the new secularist government and the former ruling Islamists and their conservative allies.
Brokers said high overnight money and repo rates continued to block cash entry to the market.
The shortage prompted by hefty public sector salary payments and money demand for the weekend caused overnight rates to keep their high levels and prompted heavy central bank funding on Friday.
The average overnight money and repo rates remained high at 73.94 and 79.93 percent, compared to Thursday's 73.79 and 79.79 percent, respectively.

"I think the bourse will wait for the results of the Treasury's first ever reverse t-bill auction on Monday. This may ease the liqudity shortage in the money market," Ibrahim Usul from Sahin Securities said.
The Treasury will open its first reverse auction to buy back bills due to mature on December 10. There are 380 trillion lira of outstanding December 10 bills in the market.

Of the 250 shares traded, 110 declined, 82 advanced and 58 ended stable. The IMKB Industrial was steady at 1,934, the IMKB Services eased 0.5 percent to 1,990 and the IMKB Financial lost 1.54 percent to 2,168.

Top actives of the day were largely state-owned flat steel producer Eregli, up 500 lira at 27,500 lira, glass producer Anadolu Cam, up 50 lira to 2,475 and Ihlas Holding, up 1,250 at 20,000. They made up 16.4 percent of the total volume.
-- Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875. KOR EKS ($ = 163640 Turkish Lire)
